Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — SecureBank is keen to move forward but our legal and infosec teams have a few non-standard asks on the DPA and the TOMs exhibit. Attached is our redline (SecureBank_DPA_redlines_20270620.pdf) and a marked TOMs exhibit with notes. High-level asks:

- BYOK / key custody: Strong preference for customer-managed keys. We would like explicit language on BYOK support, supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault), and procedures for key escrow or emergency access.
- Access controls: Explicit role-based access (separation of duties), vendor access reviews, and minimum MFA requirements for admin logins.
- Subprocessors: We require 30 days' notice and the option to object to new subprocessors that process EU customer data.
- Data transfers: Clarify the legal mechanism (SCCs + additional safeguards) and any planned reliance on UK/EU equivalents.

Please confirm who on your side will own the TOMs edits and whether you can provide the evidence we requested (SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, encryption architecture diagram).

Thanks,
Miriam
Legal — SecureBank

Hi Miriam — thanks for the detailed redlines and the TOMs markup. We're aligned on the goal of a clean, auditable arrangement. A few quick responses and next steps from our side: 

1) Ownership & next steps: I'll own point on the DPA/TOMs on behalf of Redwood. Naomi (CC'd) will coordinate evidence (SOC 2, pen test summary).

2) Keys & BYOK: Redwood supports two tracks:
   - Redwood-managed keys (default): keys generated and stored in our HSM-backed KMS; we provide audit logs, role separation, and annual key rotation by default.
   - Customer BYOK: we support customer-supplied keys via native cloud KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault). With BYOK, the customer controls key material and rotation. We can also provide a short "key-handoff" runbook for emergency decryption under strictly scoped legal process.

Can you confirm which BYOK model you prefer (full BYOK where SecureBank keeps the root key in your KMS, or a shared model where Redwood holds an envelope key)? Also: are you expecting key escrow as a hard requirement or as an optional contingency?

3) Subprocessors & notice: We can agree to 30 days' notice for new subprocessors and will offer a review period. For objection rights, enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private tiers can request additional contractual controls; let's discuss the exact escalation route (SLA/termination windows).

4) Data transfers: We use SCCs where appropriate and are preparing an additional transfer addendum that outlines technical safeguards (encryption, access controls, logging). We'll share the draft.

Attachments from our side: "TOMs_Exhibit_draft_v3.docx" (proposed edits inline), and a short response PDF. I will loop in Dev and Legal internally to confirm technical feasibility of the BYOK options.

Proposed next step: internal alignment Tuesday morning and then a 30-minute call with your team Wednesday to walk through open items. Does 10:00 AM UTC on Wed work for you?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Aisha — quick technical notes: 

- Both BYOK modes are supported in architecture; full BYOK (customer retains master key in their KMS) is supported for Dedicated/Private customers with integration work (we need to gate on networking and KMS IAM trust boundaries). Estimated engineering effort: 2 sprint tasks + one security review (roughly 3 weeks to validate and produce runbook).
- Envelope-key/shared model (Redwood holds an envelope key encrypted with customer's KMS root) is easier to support for hosted customers and provides a balance between performance and customer control.
- Rotation: our default is annual rotation for master keys with automated rewraps; we can document and support more frequent rotation on request (90 days) but this increases operational complexity and potential token cache invalidation concerns.
- Key-handoff / emergency access: we can provide a documented legal workflow (court-order or joint incident process) and an audit-traced manual unseal procedure if required by the customer; this would be executed under a strict authorization and recorded in our audit logs.
- Audit evidence: we can provide KMS audit exports (redacted), SOC 2 Type II report, and a high-level pen test summary (sensitive details redacted). Encryption architecture diagram is available and can be shared under an NDA if needed.

I'll assemble a tech appendix for the redline response and a short runbook draft.

— Dev

Miriam — thanks for your patience while we aligned internally. Below is our proposed position (we've attached a redline response PDF with inline edits). If this looks good, we'll push the DPA to DocuSign for signature.

Key points we've accepted / propose:
- BYOK & key custody: We can support full BYOK for Dedicated/Private deployments (SecureBank would hold the master key in your cloud KMS). For Hosted deployments we propose the envelope-key model. We will update the DPA and TOMs exhibit to reflect supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault) and include a short key-handoff runbook that specifies emergency access steps and required legal authorizations.
- Rotation & access: Default master key rotation: 12 months (can be shortened to 90 days by mutual agreement). All key usage is logged; we will include role-based access statements and require MFA for administrative personnel.
- Subprocessors & notice: We will provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors and a review period. For objection we propose a structured escalation (first remediation plan, then termination rights in case of material risk). This is consistent with enterprise terms.
- Evidence & transfer controls: Naomi will send SOC2 Type II and a redacted pen test summary via secure link. We will provide an updated transfer addendum that pairs SCCs with the TOMs technical safeguards.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached Redline_response_v1.pdf (contains our inline edits).
2) If agreed, we'll issue the DPA via DocuSign and put the TOMs exhibit in the same envelope. DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/ABC-ENVELOPE-7890
3) We'll also share the technical appendix (runbook + architecture diagram) under the NDA.

If you approve, please confirm and we'll route to signature today. Thanks — looking forward to getting this wrapped.

Best regards,
